title: Change Geste software and contracts
summary: Modify Geste's manual episode schema, CLI, deterministic retrieval and projections, packaging, tests, documentation, or published contracts while preserving source authority and immutable revisions.
use_when: Geste code, tests, storage, public JSON or CLI behavior, Chancery bundle, packaging, release workflow, or documentation is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary use or operation of the installed Geste CLI.
Release publication or installed deployment has not been separately authorized.
The proposed change is continuous ingestion, model-based inference, or a new source adapter without a new explicit contract review.
outcome: A minimal tested Geste change whose code, schema, read-time projections, authority boundaries, installation behavior, and published contracts agree.
effects: Modifies Geste source, tests, product documentation, packaging, release tooling, or product-owned Chancery contracts.
A schema or capture-contract change can affect persistent private state and existing manual producers.
Release and installed deployment remain separate effects.
authority: Geste owns episode identity, immutable revision storage, authored interpretation, validation, retrieval, projections, and product packaging.
Cited products remain authoritative for upstream records; Geste changes may not copy their bodies or imply current verification.
A historical episode never becomes current procedure merely through implementation or retrieval behavior.
success: The smallest owning code and exact architecture, CLI, data-model, installation, and Chancery contracts agree.

Tests preserve strict capture, atomic append, revision immutability, deterministic latest-head search, historical reads, report and graph derivation, privacy, content identity, and rollback as affected.
Schema changes include an explicit migration, quiescent backup boundary, old-state fixture, and database-aware rollback rather than implicit migration.
failure_and_recovery: Do not weaken validation, rewrite an old revision, infer causality from time, or elevate a locator-only anchor or unverified settlement to authority.
Keep automatic ingestion and source resolution out of manual v0.1 unless a later reviewed contract assigns exact ownership and recovery.
Packaging changes retain content identity, provider/version matching, foreign-state refusal, stable selectors, and post-switch rollback.
privacy: Fixtures must be synthetic; source, provider, release, logs, and examples must contain no real episode database or private source body.
Diagnostics should avoid echoing capture prose, source labels, and machine-specific identities.
steps: Read Geste's product instructions and exact architecture, CLI, data-model, installation, and Chancery contracts affected by the change.
Identify whether the change alters episode authority, storage, capture compatibility, retrieval ranking, privacy, recovery, or another product's boundary before editing.
Implement the smallest change with synthetic isolated fixtures and update every exact product-owned contract in the same change.
Run `geste/ci.sh`; run release or deployment only under separate authority.
checkpoints: Manual v0.1 retains no runtime dependency on another Cell product, model, service, or network.
Create and revise remain complete immutable snapshots, with stale-base and verified-settlement validation fail-closed.
Search and read-time graph/report output remain deterministic and do not claim semantic analogy or current source truth.
Deployment never initializes or migrates the domain database.
adaptation: Add source-specific runtime integration only after a new boundary review names source identity, cutoff, errors, privacy, and recovery.
Treat continuous ingestion as a later product contract, not an incremental shortcut inside manual capture.
stop_when: The change would silently duplicate another product's authority or recast episode interpretation as verified truth.
A persistent-state change lacks explicit migration and rollback proof.
The requested behavior cannot be represented within Geste's reviewed manual v0.1 boundary.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Deploying an installed Geste release or initializing a user database.
Changing, invoking, or reading another Cell product beyond separately selected installed contracts.

consumers.statement: An interactive contributor may change Geste within its reviewed manual-casebook boundary while keeping product contracts and tests synchronized.

preconditions.statement: The contributor has read Geste instructions and affected public contracts, identified the owning boundary, and has separate authority before any release or deployment.

inputs.statement: Inputs are the requested scoped change, current Geste source and public contracts, synthetic fixtures, and any explicitly selected installed documentation contracts.

outputs.statement: The output is the smallest synchronized source, test, documentation, packaging, or provider change with a green Geste CI result.

data_semantics.statement: Development preserves episode-authored interpretation, immutable complete revisions, source-owner authority, deterministic projections, and the distinction between a historical case and current procedure.

identity_and_units.statement: Existing public episode, revision, capture-schema, database-schema, and release identities retain their documented meanings unless an explicit successor is introduced.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completion covers every affected Geste code, test, architecture, CLI, data-model, installation, and Chancery contract and the current CI run.

access.statement: Development uses the local repository filesystem and shell; access to another product requires its separately selected installed contract.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Persistent changes require explicit migration, quiescent backup, old-state proof, and database-aware rollback; release and deployment remain later separate transitions.

operational_limits.statement: The operation is bounded to Geste's short-lived manual v0.1 product and must stop before continuous ingestion, model inference, or an unreviewed source adapter.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Incompatible capture, storage, source, or packaging meaning receives an explicit new contract or migration while historical revisions remain readable.

reliances.statement: Geste development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
This terminology authority does not create a represented-product runtime reliance of the development operation.
